questions.q: What question was Priya from Lesson 1 actually asking, that this lesson finally answers?
options: Has anyone actually restored a backup, not just confirmed one exists
How much does Azure SQL Database cost per month
Which service tier should the database use
How many tables exist in the Patients database
questions.explain: Lesson 1's scare was that nobody had ever tested a restore — this lesson is where that gap finally gets closed with a real, tested restore.

questions.q: How does Azure SQL Database's point-in-time restore relate to the on-prem WITH NORECOVERY / WITH RECOVERY chained restore pattern?
options: Azure performs that same chained logic internally and automatically — you give it one timestamp instead of orchestrating each restore step by hand
Azure SQL Database doesn't support point-in-time restore at all, only full restores
WITH NORECOVERY and WITH RECOVERY are required flags on the az sql db restore command
The chained logic only applies to differential backups, never to log backups
questions.explain: The NORECOVERY/RECOVERY distinction doesn't disappear — Azure is doing exactly that chained restore logic internally, just automated behind a single point-in-time operation.

questions.q: What does a point-in-time restore on Azure SQL Database actually produce?
options: An entirely new, separate database alongside the original — the original is never overwritten
The original database restored in place, overwriting its current contents
A read-only snapshot that cannot be queried
A downloadable .bak file for manual restoration elsewhere
questions.explain: The restore always creates a new database. This is a deliberate safety design — you verify the restored copy before deciding how to use it, without ever risking the original.

questions.q: In the `az sql db restore` command, what does `--dest-name` specify?
options: The name of the new database the restore creates
The name of the original database being restored from
The destination resource group for the restore
The destination Azure region for the restored database
questions.explain: --dest-name names the new database the restore operation produces — there's no option to restore in place over the original.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call this restore test 'the single most important lab in the whole project'?
options: It's what actually turns a backup plan into a tested backup plan, closing the exact gap Lesson 1 identified
It's the only lesson that uses the Azure CLI instead of the Portal
It's the most expensive operation in the entire capstone
It's the only lab that requires deleting the original database first
questions.explain: Everything before this lesson built toward one real, verified restore — the difference between a backup that's assumed to work and one that's actually been proven to.
